sources.entry: Tyk - Fast and scalable open source API Gateway. Out of the box, Tyk offers an API Management Platform with an API Gateway, API Analytics, Developer Portal and API Management Dashboard. (Source Code) MPL-2.0 Go/Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: Tyk Gateway is an open source, Go-based API and AI gateway that handles REST, GraphQL, TCP, gRPC, SOAP and MCP traffic with auth, rate limiting, analytics and transformation.
summary.what_it_does: Tyk Gateway sits in front of upstream APIs and applies middleware such as authentication (JWT, bearer tokens, Basic Auth, client certificates), rate limiting and quotas, and per-version or per-operation access control. It can import Swagger/OpenAPI documents (OAS 2.x and 3.0.1) to scaffold APIs, and can generate an MCP proxy from a REST API. It also parses JSON-RPC 2.0 for MCP traffic so policy applies per tool, resource and prompt. Content mediation lets it rewrite headers or convert between SOAP and GraphQL. Plugins can be written in Python, JavaScript, Go, or any gRPC-capable language. Configuration can be reloaded without interrupting active requests. The README also points to separate OSS components: Tyk Pump for analytics export, Tyk Identity Broker for third-party login, and Tyk AI Studio (AGPL-3.0) for LLM management.
use_cases: Put rate limits and API keys in front of internal or partner APIs
Govern MCP traffic from AI agents with per-tool access control
Import OpenAPI or Swagger specs to create gateway APIs
Convert SOAP services to GraphQL or rewrite request and response headers
Run a Kubernetes-native API gateway with Helm
Record API usage analytics and send webhooks on quota or auth failures
how_to_run: Create a tyk.conf gateway configuration file and an apps folder (on Linux)
Create a Docker Compose file that runs Tyk Gateway and Redis
Start the gateway with: docker compose up -d
To build from source: git clone the repo, then run go build (Go version from go.mod)
notable: Batteries-included open source gateway with no feature lockout
Parses MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 and applies policy per tool, resource and prompt
Generates MCP proxies directly from REST APIs
Hitless reloads of configuration without dropping active requests
Dual-licensed: MPL-2.0 for core code, commercial license for the ee folder
caveats: Official support is limited to Linux/amd64, Linux/i386 and Linux/arm64
Tests require Redis running locally on the default port
The Tyk Operator Kubernetes integration requires a licence
The full management dashboard, developer portal and enterprise platform are separate commercial offerings (Tyk Self Managed or Tyk Cloud)
keywords: put a gateway in front of my api
